items.reason: The sync branch returns a raw Fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific token objects or .data fields, breaking refresh.
Google Calendar stores the safeParse wrapper as the credential key instead of the parsed token data, corrupting subsequent credential reads.
Zoho Bigin passes the credential row ID instead of the owner's user ID, sending the wrong calcomUserId to the sync endpoint.
The computed Zod property names create literal keys rather than wildcard validators, so the sync schema fails to preserve intended expiry fields.
The Salesforce credential update references prisma without importing it, causing type-checking and runtime failures.
Salesforce refreshes tokens unconditionally on service construction, adding a network request and database write even when the saved token remains valid.
